properties.inspection_comments: Purpose: To conduct a food safety inspection in accordance with WAC Chapter 246-215. Due to 35 or more red points, a follow-up inspection will be conducted for the red item violations noted in this inspection report. A fee of $240 will be assessed by mail for all follow-up inspections. If repeated red item violations are observed at a follow-up inspection, an additional follow-up inspection will be required. Notes: - Replace batteries of digital probe thermometer and ensure that back-up thermometers are kept in kitchen area to monitor temperatures. - Securely affix soap dispenser to wall above handwash sink . - Facility has removed ice machine from back kitchen prep area. If facility wishes to reinstall ice machine in the future, contact food@tpchd.org prior to installation. - Discussed that facility requires a certified food protection manager(CFPM) and that certificate must remain on site and available for review during inspection. If facility does not have a current CFPM, links to different accredited CFPM courses will be included in inspection report email . Compliance Schedule OBSERVATIONS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS You must complete the following items by the due date listed below . Your inspector will do a compliance inspection . If these items are not corrected, you will be billed for the inspection. Violations cited must be corrected within the time frames specified . Complete ByItem Number 09/18/2026 2600 Compliance with valid permit; operating and risk control plans and required written procedures. 2600 Observed the following: - Facility's floor plan lists a 1- door True Countertop cooler in service area . Facility's temperature list has included 1-door countertop cooler in service area since 2023, but facility has since removed it and returned to cold holding on ice/with ice packs, carafes, etc. -Per facility's approval letter: Mechanical refrigeration is required to remain functional and in use. No ice only cold holding. -No alterations to the approved plans, equipment, and menu can be made without prior TPCHD approval . Facility must operate as approved. To operate as approved facility must : - Reinstall 1-door countertop cooler in service area for use in cold holding. - Submit an updated floor plan and equipment list for review to health department. *A compliance order has been issued to reinstall the removed 1-door True countertop cooler in service area by 09/18/2026. If installing a replacement, ensure the replacement is of commercial or NSF grade and of equal or greater capacity. Failure to reinstall the removed 1- door True countertop cooler in service area by 09/18/2026 will result in a $240 non-compliance fee. Contact your inspector with questions or if you need more time to complete these items. Tacoma - Pierce County Health Department 3629 South D Street, MS 1059 Tacoma , WA 98418 Fax: (253) 649-1728Inspector : Dylan Caverly

A fee of $240 will be assessed by mail for all follow-up inspections. If repeated red item violations are observed at a follow-up inspection, an additional follow-up inspection will be required Notes: - Ensure when employees are doing temperature checks they are checking food temperatures in the units and not just the unit read outs as they are not always accurate. If TCS foods are found cold holding above 42F or above, ensure to document corrective actions taken. For example, if TCS foods are found cold holding 42-45F, foods should be relocated to functional unit to cool and unit monitored. If TCS foods are found cold holding 45F or above, discard foods and notify maintenance to service unit. Compliance Schedule OBSERVATIONS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS You must complete the following items by the due date listed below . Your inspector will do a compliance inspection . If these items are not corrected, you will be billed for the inspection. Violations cited must be corrected within the time frames specified . Complete ByItem Number 09/09/2026 2120 Proper cold holding temperatures (10 pts if more than 45F). 2120 Observed the following: - 2 Door Prep Top Cooler : (top) hardboiled eggs 61-64F (in pan on top of drop in pans) - 2 door Trauslen reach in cooler : cottage cheese 49F, commercial ranch 48F, milk 48F, whipped cream 55F, yogurt 45F, ambient 47F All Time /Temperature Control for Safety Food (TCS) must be cold held at 41°F or below at all times. Hardboiled eggs discarded. Ensure not to stock foods on top of drop in pans in top of prep top cooler. Cold held foods must be fully in unit to be maintained properly. Cottage cheese, milk, and whipped cream discarded at PIC discretion. All other foods in 2 door Trauslen reach in cooler were relocated to funcitonal unit in main kitchen area. Adjust or repair 2 door Trauslen reach in cooler to cold hold at 41F or below. If unit cannot be adjusted or repaired, replace unit with unit that is commercial grade and of equal or greater capacity. Do not store any TCS food in unit until unit is consistently cold holding at 41F or below. ------------------------------------------- Observed the following: - Walk In Cooler : hot dogs 45F (recent use), commercial mashed potatoes 44F, commercial hardboiled eggs 45F, cut cabbage 45F, liquid egg 45F, gyro meat 44F, heavy cream 45F, cut watermelon 45F, feta 44F, ambient 45F All Time /Temperature Control for Safety Food (TCS) must be cold held at 41°F or below at all times. Adjust or repair walk-in cooler to cold hold at 41F or below. On site maintenance contacted to adjust or repair unit. No cooling of hot foods permitted until unit is consistently cold holding at 41F or below. If unit rises above 45F contact your inspector for guidance. *Compliance order issued to adjust or repair walk-in cooler to cold hold at 41F or below by 9/9/2026. Failure to repair or adjust unit to cold hold consistently at 41F or below by 9/9/2026 will result in a fee of $240 for non-compliance and potential closure of facility until unit is repaired. Contact your inspector with questions or if you need more time to complete these items.
